clue.text: Emergent clique's 18th

parts.note: something emergent is in the act of emerging, appearing from cover
a clique is an exclusive set of people, a faction or party

explanation.surface: A secretive little group celebrates an eighteenth birthday as it emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: '18th' reads as an ordinal or a date, but it is the definition: a debutante's presentation to society traditionally came at eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante's formal launch into society, the traditional celebration when a girl turned eighteen, so an eighteenth birthday party.

clue.text: Evaluating business scam

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a sting is a confidence trick or swindle

explanation.surface: Someone is assessing a fraudulent business operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out what something will cost is a way of assessing or pricing it.

clue.text: Result of too many a medieval banquet?

definitions.text: Result of too many a medieval banquet?

parts.words: Result of too many a medieval banquet
parts.note: medieval suggests a period of history and a banquet a lavish meal, but read as midlife years and a feast the outcome is a thickening waistline

explanation.surface: Overindulging at feasts in a castle hall would have consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sends you to the period of history; the answer is the thickening waist that arrives in one's forties or fifties, a 'spread' doubling as a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: The weight gained around the middle in midlife, punningly linked to feasting in a bygone era.

clue.text: Never take pole to a railway

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Advice never to carry a pole along a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect word meaning not one, used in phrases like 'nary a word', so never.

clue.text: Fancy old sailors getting fed up!

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors
ate up, consumed, as one who has fed

explanation.surface: Elderly seamen growing weary of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as weary, but here it means ate up, consumed. The definition 'Fancy' is an adjective, elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy in the sense of elaborately decorated, highly embellished.

clue.text: One willing to check retirement list

parts.note: to test is to check

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the word for a duty list is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Someone happy to examine the list of people due to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One willing' looks like a volunteer, but it is one who makes a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes a will, literally one doing the willing of an estate.

clue.text: Hostile article by sibling? Quite the opposite!

parts.note: anti means opposed or hostile to
the is the definite article
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: Is a sibling actually hostile? Not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct contrary, the exact reverse of something.

clue.text: Reveal how ill-gotten art goes astray

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Explaining how stolen artwork disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes astray' rearranges the letters of HOW ILLGOTTEN ART, all fifteen of them, into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak frankly and disclose things someone needs to hear, so to reveal or inform.

clue.text: Make time to see old W. German chancellor

parts.note: a make is a brand of product

explanation.surface: Arranging time to visit a former West German leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy Brandt was Chancellor of West Germany from 1969 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt led the Federal Republic of Germany as its chancellor.

clue.text: Levelling implement for roads in disrepair

indicators.note: in disrepair means broken down, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A tool for flattening broken-down roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' of 'in disrepair' is part of the fodder: ROADS IN is rearranged, signalled by 'disrepair'. A sadiron is an old flat iron heated on a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy flatiron for pressing clothes smooth, a smoothing tool.

clue.text: Pioneer clearly not indebted

definitions.meaning: a colonist who makes a home in new territory
one who has settled up and paid off what is owed

explanation.definitionFit: A colonist who sets up home in new land, and punningly one who settles accounts.

clue.text: Tick over despite being work-shy

definitions.meaning: of an engine, to run slowly while out of gear

explanation.definitionFit: An engine running without driving anything, and a lazy person avoiding labour.

clue.text: Squad beset by stress needs transport

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the word for squad sits inside the word for stress

parts.note: strain is stress or tension
a team is a squad of players

explanation.surface: An overworked team requires a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive-hauled train powered by steam is a means of conveyance.

clue.text: Consider it's intentional

definitions.meaning: to think something over carefully, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for weighing a matter up, and an adjective for something done on purpose.

clue.text: Gang-leader goes mad for claret

parts.note: the leading letter of the word gang
raves means rants wildly, as if mad

explanation.surface: A gang boss loses his temper over a Bordeaux wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux; Graves is a Bordeaux district and its wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bordeaux wine region whose reds are sold as claret.

clue.text: How teams play? Rather!

indicators.note: play suggests loose movement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone asks how the teams are playing and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' signals the rearrangement of HOW TEAMS. 'Rather!' looks like an exclamation of agreement, but here it means to some degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to a moderate degree, fairly.

clue.text: Way to display Islamic symbol

definitions.meaning: a curved street, often used in British road names
the curved moon shape emblematic of Islam

explanation.definitionFit: A curving street name, and the crescent moon used as an emblem of Islam.

clue.text: Barry, I've mislaid the prayer book

indicators.note: mislaid suggests things put in the wrong place, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone tells Barry they have lost the prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' signals the rearrangement of BARRY and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breviary is a book of daily offices said by Catholic clergy, a liturgical book.

clue.text: What he wants is a lot

definitions.text: What he wants is a lot

parts.words: What he wants is a lot
parts.note: a lot looks like a great deal, but at an auction a lot is an item up for sale that this person hopes to win

explanation.surface: A greedy man wants plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' means a great deal on the surface; at an auction it is an item put up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at an auction offering money for an item listed for sale.

clue.text: Champ from west central

parts.note: inner means central, towards the middle

explanation.surface: A champion from the centre of the western region.
explanation.definitionFit: A champ is short for champion, the victor.

clue.text: Top-class author's fee

definitions.meaning: the highest rank of society, kings and queens
a payment to a writer for each copy sold

explanation.definitionFit: The monarch and family as society's highest rank, and a percentage paid to a writer on sales.

clue.text: Car taken to old city with little demur

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
er is a small hesitant sound expressing doubt

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly agrees to drive a car to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring car is a large open motor car built for long journeys.

clue.text: Black dog's bowl

definitions.meaning: Churchill's phrase for his bouts of melancholy; the 's stands for is
a hollow or dip in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Black dog is a nickname for low mood, and a bowl is a hollow in a surface.

clue.text: Curious to know if lad returned before may's end

indicators.note: before places the boy's word ahead of the final letter
returned means sent back, so the word for a boy is read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy, a lad

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a boy came home before the end of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SON into NOS; 'may's end' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inquisitive and prying into others' affairs.

clue.text: Does parliament pass them?

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning performs, and the laws a parliament enacts.

clue.text: Give promotion to raise the spirits

definitions.meaning: to move someone up in rank
to cheer up, lift the mood

explanation.definitionFit: To move someone up a rank, and to lift someone's mood.

clue.text: Telling poor Clare to hold it

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word it goes inside the rearranged name
poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clare's version of the story is a weak one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' looks like a verb or adjective, but it is a noun here, an account given aloud or in order; 'poor' scrambles the name and 'to hold' wraps it round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed account or narration of events.

clue.text: Commercial projects by right-winger? That's a tale!

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
ventures are enterprises or projects
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative's business schemes are dismissed as fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative of exciting and dangerous exploits is a kind of story.
